name: Parrish Art Museum
funding: $6.1M expenses (2023); Hamptons donors, Bank of America, J.P. Morgan Private Bank, Related, Suffolk County, NYSCA and IMLS.
watch: Bloomberg Philanthropies, a name under campaign, is on the 2024 donor list ($20k-49k). No protest at the museum found.
records_note: Annual reports 2017 to 2025 and audited statements are on its site, a named 2024 donor list is public, and trustees are listed.

name: Fondazione Pastificio Cerere
funding: Fondazione Pastificio Cerere Onlus, Italian Ministry of Culture, Regione Lazio; non-profit foundation.

name: Pejman Foundation (Argo Factory)
funding: Private non-profit founded in 2015 by collector and film producer Hamidreza Pejman, who bought the Argo Factory brewery in 2016.
watch: Argo Factory is closed until further notice; the war began on 28 February 2026. Pejman says an unnamed body shut its film series over permits.
records_note: Argo Factory names three in-kind sponsors on an undated page, and lists staff but no board; no reports or accounts are published.

name: Pera Museum
watch: Whether the foundation holds Koç assets is unknown.
records_note: The Suna and Inan Kirac Foundation posts a 2025 activity report and names its six-member board; no donor list or audited accounts found.

name: Perm State Art Gallery
funding: Regional state (GKBUK; founder Ministry of Culture of Perm Krai); new 21,000 sq m building in the Zavod Shpagina cluster financed by the region, move completed Feb 2026.
watch: Director Yulia Tavrizyan; sponsor list not published on the site.
records_note: Posts a 2025 results report and 2025 financial results report, with plans back to 2022; no sponsor list and no board.

name: PERMM Museum of Contemporary Art
funding: Regional state (GKBUK; founder Ministry of Culture of Perm Krai); founded 2009 under governor Chirkunov with Marat Gelman and sponsor Sergei Gordeev; new building on Krisanova St since 2024.
watch: FSB searched the museum and director Nailya Allakhverdieva's home on 21 Nov 2024 in the 'terrorism justification' case against founder Gelman (declared foreign agent 2021, listed as terrorist/extremist 2024); museum closed one day. Prosecutor filed a conflict-of-interest suit against the director in Oct 2024; an earlier search in Mar 2024. Allakhverdieva left; Elena Novikova appointed.
records_note: A regional state museum: its Documents page posts results reports 2019 to 2025 with a balance sheet; it names no funders and no board.

name: Petach Tikva Museum of Art
funding: Friends association (2015) funds shows and acquisitions via 1,800 NIS memberships and a 23,000 NIS patron tier. British Friends of the Art Museums of Israel back programmes. No budget published.
watch: In 2014 the municipality called on the museum to close Arkadi Zaides's Archive; the New York Review of Books reports the museum refused.
records_note: The Friends association board is listed with Reut Ferster as chair; the museum publishes no reports, accounts or donor names.

name: PICA Perth
funding: Revenue A$2.84M and 169,720 visitors (2024). WA Government through DLGSC with Lotterywest, Creative Australia, City of Perth and Minderoo Foundation, which backs Hatched and two staff roles.
watch: Minderoo holds the Forrests' $5B Fortescue gift. On 12 May 2026 the Federal Court ordered Fortescue to pay the Yindjibarndi $150M for Solomon Hub.
records_note: Posts annual reports from 2006 with financial statements, a named 2024 donor list and partners, and names its directors.

name: PICA Portland
funding: $2.5M expenses (FY2025). Oregon Arts Commission, City of Portland, Warhol, Ford, Mellon, Meyer Trust and Kinsman foundations; Nike, Netflix, Google. Pacific Power Foundation and NW Natural also give.
records_note: Posts a 2025 impact report and names its board, with sponsor logos for the 2026 TBA festival; Form 990s for 2002 to 2025 on ProPublica.

name: Picha / Lubumbashi Biennale
funding: Founders' own money, private donors and Belgian and French agencies. 2026 Biennale sponsors: Belgian foreign ministry, Wallonie-Bruxelles, Enabel, Africalia, Pullman, Africell, TMB bank.
watch: Artist-led; urgent funding call in August 2026.
records_note: Shows the 2026 Biennale sponsors as a page of logos and lists its curators and staff, but publishes no reports, accounts or board.

name: Pier Arts Centre
funding: £618k income (FY2025). Creative Scotland and Orkney Islands Council; partner of Tate through the Plus Tate network.
watch: Collection founded by Margaret Gardiner's gift. No flagged funder or protest found.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the OSCR register, the Partnerships page names funders and partners undated, and the board is listed.

name: Pinault Collection (Bourse de Commerce)
funding: Privately endowed by French luxury billionaire François Pinault (founder of Kering luxury conglomerate: Gucci, Saint Laurent, Balenciaga).
watch: A prestige vehicle for a private luxury-goods group: it works as a brand showcase for Kering's luxury holdings and receives large state tax deductions.
